function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We need to use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command. On Windows, we can check if Chrome is installed by checking the existence of the executable path. Usually Chrome is installed at "C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" or "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe". We can use the 'where' command: where chrome.exe. That will return the path if found. So we can call cmd_controller_execute with command: "where chrome.exe". That will output the path(s). If not found, it will error. But we can capture output. The tool returns whatever os.system returns? Actually os.system returns exit status. But we might not get output. But we can still call it. The tool's signature: command: string, unit?: string. So we can call with command: "where chrome.exe". Let's do that.
